description: Multi-objective label correcting finds one path for every Pareto-optimal cost vector. A cost vector is *Pareto-optimal* when no other path is as good in every objective and better in one. Each state keeps a set of non-dominated labels (partial paths with their cost vectors). A first-in, first-out queue holds the states whose set changed. The algorithm extends the new labels of a queued state along each edge and merges them into the successors' sets; unlike label setting, a label can be dropped after it was extended. It needs no heuristic and is exact for non-negative edge costs.

papers.title: Label Correcting Methods to Solve Multicriteria Shortest Path Problems
papers.venue: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications

papers.authors: Oren Salzman, Carlos Hernández Ulloa, Ariel Felner, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Multi-Objective Search: Algorithms, Applications, and Emerging Directions
